project.name: ClapControl IoT
project.context: ESP32 local web dashboard for relay control and KY-037 analog threshold calibration
project.runtime: PlatformIO Arduino on ESP32 DevKit V1
constraints: Use KY-037 AO on GPIO34 for web threshold
Use KY-037 DO on GPIO35 as diagnostic state

motionPaletteDecision.anchorReference: digital peak programme meter with threshold marker
motionPaletteDecision.motionBehavior: Live level responds quickly while peak-hold marker decays more slowly and threshold marker moves immediately.
motionPaletteDecision.paletteBehavior: Amber marks threshold, green marks relay power, blue marks peak memory, and red is reserved for destructive off/error states.
motionPaletteDecision.typographicRoleContrast: Large tabular ADC numbers contrast with compact uppercase hardware labels.

productReading.productTypeAndCoreVerb: Embedded IoT control panel where the user calibrates sound threshold and switches a relay.
productReading.highestStakesMoments: The highest stakes are seeing threshold crossing, forcing relay state, and avoiding double toggle from one clap.
productReading.dominantDataShapes: The screen is dominated by telemetry, a threshold boundary, binary relay state, and small numeric controls.
productReading.latencyProfile: The interface is soft real-time because it polls ESP32 status several times per second.
productReading.failureModes: The UI must absorb offline dashboard, noisy sensor, too-high threshold, relay polarity mismatch, and unsafe bulb wiring.
productReading.contextOfUse: The dashboard is used during bench testing on a phone or laptop in the same WiFi network.
productReading.knownConstraints: The UI is embedded HTML/CSS/JS with no external libraries and must remain light enough for ESP32 flash/RAM.

derivedTokenLogic.anchorReference: digital peak programme meter with threshold marker
derivedTokenLogic.colorDerivationSource: Signal roles: threshold amber, peak blue, relay green, danger red, graphite casing.
derivedTokenLogic.spacingDerivationSource: Meter and controls are separated like instrument display and calibration controls.
derivedTokenLogic.typographyDerivationSource: Large tabular numbers carry sensor state; compact labels carry hardware mapping.
derivedTokenLogic.motionDerivationSource: Live level follows ADC updates; peak marker decays slowly for calibration memory.
derivedTokenLogic.typeScaleMethod: Fixed role scale with clamp on headline only
derivedTokenLogic.validationRule: Every visual token must improve relay control, threshold calibration, or sensor confidence.

libraryDecisions.name: Native CSS and browser fetch API
libraryDecisions.purpose: Serve a dependency-free dashboard from ESP32 flash.
libraryDecisions.risk: No component library behavior is available, so accessibility must be implemented directly.
libraryDecisions.fallbackIfUnavailable: HTML controls and JSON endpoints remain operable.

locked: WiFi local dashboard must stay available

aiSafeUiAudit.renameTestRule: If the page still works as a finance dashboard or generic smart-home app without changing composition, revise.

tokenSystem.format: CSS custom properties in embedded stylesheet

colorTruth.statusColorRule: Color is never the only state signal; text labels must repeat relay, trigger, and DO state.

crossViewportAdaptation.desktop: Meter and controls sit side by side for sustained calibration.
crossViewportAdaptation.tablet: Controls remain near the meter while secondary telemetry compresses.
crossViewportAdaptation.mobile: Signal meter appears first, then relay controls, then calibration sliders.

motionSystem.signatureMove: Analog fill moves quickly while peak hold decays slowly.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: Transitions collapse through prefers-reduced-motion while numeric values still update.
motionSystem.budget: High-frequency state changes stay under short CSS transitions.

componentMorphology.surfaceModel: Instrument panels with stable dimensions and 8px radius.
componentMorphology.controlModel: Large touch buttons and native range sliders.
componentMorphology.stateModel: Text plus color state for relay, trigger, DO, and connection.
